question: A 40-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of a painless lump on his neck. Two years ago, he underwent surgery for treatment-resistant hypertension, episodic headaches, and palpitations. Physical examination shows a firm, irregular swelling on the right side of the neck. Ultrasonography of the thyroid gland shows a 2-cm nodule with irregular margins and microcalcifications in the right thyroid lobe. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show increased serum concentration of which of the following substances?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Thyroid nodule with irregular margins and microcalcifications -> Suspicion of thyroid cancer -> Possible increase in Calcitonin levels -> 70%
analysis: Given the patient's presentation of a painless lump on the neck, history of surgery for hypertension, headaches, and palpitations, along with the findings of a thyroid nodule with irregular margins and microcalcifications, the most likely diagnosis is thyroid cancer, specifically medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). MTC is associated with elevated serum calcitonin levels. Therefore, further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show an increased serum concentration of calcitonin.
